text:
jules: heads up — after the canary today we saw a ~4x p50 spike when loading the 64-shard Llama-3 variant. looks like warmup stalled on shard index reads.
anya: ugh, same cluster? which path (safetensors vs tarball)?
jules: safetensors, manifestless layout (we fallback to scanning headers). logs show lots of small reads and stall waiting on 6 hot files.
ben: can you paste the relevant log slice? wondering if it's just cold filesystem metadata.
jules: sure — relevant excerpt:
```
2026-03-18T14:02:11Z loader: opening s0.safetensors
2026-03-18T14:02:11Z loader: reading header idx 0..8192
2026-03-18T14:02:11Z loader: blocked on open(s6.safetensors) (io wait 120ms)
2026-03-18T14:02:11Z warmup: pending prefetch tasks=64 inflight=6
```
mike: inflight=6 feels like our current shard-per-thread prefetch cap. if several shards hit the same disk, metadata ops serialize.
kai: idea: implement a "delayed-merge loader" — first read a tiny index from every shard (async, low-bandwidth), merge index in-memory, then schedule bulk mmap/pread for contiguous ranges. reduces metadata thrash.
anya: that sounds similar to index-first but slightly different from our current "manifest-first" path. what's the tradeoff? more round trips vs fewer concurrent opens? 
ben: also need to consider manifest vs manifestless: with manifest we do one metadata read; without we currently scan each file's header which causes N opens. delayed-merge could batch the header reads into a single step and prioritize hot tensors.
jules: prototype sketch:
```
// phase 1: metadata probe
for shard in shards:
  async read_header(shard, small_buffer)
merge_headers()
// phase 2: schedule heavy reads grouped by file offsets
for hot_segment in sorted(hot_segments):
  schedule_bulk_read(hot_segment)
```
mike: how would eviction / early-evict interact? If large models don't fully warm, we should avoid pinning whole shards.
kai: keep small evictable regions; treat hot_segments as advise-mmap + madvise(MADV_WILLNEED) but with timeouts.
anya: performance question — do we save latency on first token? p50 went up which suggests blocking during decode start.
ben: yes, if decoder waits on key-value cache warmup we see p50 blips. delayed-merge reduces blocking by ensuring the first few KV ranges are scheduled first.
jules: edge case: quantized blobs where header size is small but the tensor layout requires different alignment. need robust header parser.
mike: also consider concurrent clients — we should dedupe header probes across requests for the same model version.
anya: +1 to dedupe. also prefer serving path to expose pluggable strategies (manifest, index-first, delayed-merge). add a flag per model in catalog.
ben: operational concern: how do we observe this? propose two new metrics: header_probe_latency and merged_index_time, plus gauge dedupe_hits.
kai: I'll add a perf test: 64-shard, 128 concurrent requests, NFS vs local ext4, compare manifestless current vs delayed-merge.
deploy-bot: canary deployment queued for eng-ml/canary-3 at 2026-03-19T03:00:00Z — tag: delayed-merge-probe
jules: thanks. next steps: kai + ben to run perf runs, mike to add dedupe cache, anya to spec model-catalog toggle. i'll open a short RFC doc after we have numbers. :thumbsup:
ben: sounds good — if perf wins, we should fold into warmup pipeline and add a safety fallback to current scan.
mike: one more: update loader telemetry to include shard_open_failures so SRE can alert on excessive metadata waits.
anya: noted. i'll add to the rollout checklist. 
jules: cool. blocking items: prototype results and a tiny RFC by EOW.
